reviews.content: It's day one, so I will try to update to reflect later thoughts! So far the interface is easy to use and I like the reading it has for relevant concerns. I am genuinely looking forward to using this tomorrow! 😊 I do wish the courses had a night mode or a different background. Just a little glaring nitpick though, otherwise I think it is pretty good.

A pretty good mental health app. It was really hard to find a free one that was what I'm looking for, and I think this is very close, but not quite it, which is why only 3 stars. I do entries and questions every day, but what I thought were the best were the lessons and audio things. However, it only gives you one of each free. So now it is more of a nothing app now that those are over, but if you pour money into it, this could potentially be a 5 star app.

The app needs a few more log options. i went to log 'had a workout today' but that wasnt available, however 'had sex was'. Both are prettybcommon things but I've expirerenced this problem before. Its not a big deal, you can simply add your situation but I thought I'd point it out. the daily questions also get really repetitive. overall it's a really good app so far

I used the unpaid version and that still offers a lot. I like that it makes you check in with yourself through the day, it helps with awareness. Then it gives you sort of articles and meditation specifically for what you're struggling with. My problem was, the voice they used for the meditations, I found it SO unsettling. It's supposed to be calming, but the pitch/timbre of the voice of this man whispering to me. It made me more anxious, I couldn't use it. I wish they had other voices.

This app is fantastic. It's very simple and doesn't take a long time to figure out or use. Works great and there is a lot of information on depression--causes and solutions. Even offers different ways to get in touch with a therapist or helpline. There are many articles and exercises to read but only a few are free (otherwise you must pay for premium version). The free ones are still a nice introduction.

Very helpful when it comes to tracking my emotions! My only complaint is that the questionnaire pops up at the exact same times every day, rather than adjusting to when I last answered questions. It would be beneficial for there to be a 4 hour gap between questions, regardless of when we answer them, because sometimes I won't fill it out for three hours, but then the next set of questions pops up an hour later, which isn't a good gauge of the whole day.

It was 5 stars before I realized some I formation you can only get through a "meditation." I would rather put mashed potatoes in my ear than have someone talk to me like that. So far I have not seen an option to read the info. Besides that I really like the app and I see myself using it long term as long as I don't keep running into that tone.

I really like this app, and it has a lot of helpful features for me to track my progress. But every time I click a notification on the app, it has me enter the review in twice. Once to write a note, then again to answer the questions and then I have to write the more again. It's frustrating when I forget this, write a long note, only to have it erased and have to write everything again.

I have only been able to use the journal. I like that it reminds me when I need to journal...and relax...but because if financial constraints I can't use any other part of the app. 😞 ..but if it helps I'd really like too.....I'm interested in all of the courses because most of them is what I'm experiencing every day ....it's a really neat ce app you did a great job...!! I just can't afford it...

This is very useful for tracking your mood through each day, and it reminds you to enter info regularly. Each update offers an opportunity to enter your thoughts at the time its checking in (3x a day for me), which is great for finding repeating patterns and addressing them. If I could request an improvement, it would be secure, private cloud-syncing account. I would love if I could answer the questions and access my records on any device. I would 5 star this!

Looked like it could actually be really helpful with the two-week tracking and depression/anxiety scales, but I never even got that far since the first thing you have to do is accept a "privacy" policy that includes, among other things, using your data for Facebook advertising and anonymous research. The latter is not a huge issue with me, but it could be with others. I definitely have an issue with using my data on a very personal app for advertising, though--especially when there's no obvious way out. Disappointing. At least the policy was transparent and in plain language, have to give the developers that much.

Pretty good so far, the daily questions are pretty helpful and keep you aware of the days progress and events and I find it very grounding. I'd give it a 5 star but because they only ask you like, 5 questions and limited/the same options for how you are feeling, i find it for lack if better words, discouraging. I do reccomend this app though because it helps with journaling if you can't keep up with it in a book or it's hard to filter/slow your thoughts enough to get them on to paper (me)

I like the app BUT find many of the questions, I'm feeling a certain way due to a physical disability, and don't necessarily feel as emotionally stressed as physically- wish there was a way to distinguish. Also, it would be nice if all three times could be customized. The second set always pops up halfway through my workday, and I'm not allowed to have my phone on me, so i miss all of the midday questions.

Very helpful for helping me recognize patterns and feelings im having and good for recording events and how they affected me and my mood on a daily basis. I like it also because it checks in with you and notifys you instead of me trying to remember to do it on a daily basis. The therapy that they refer you to though doesnt seem very realistic though in a sense and cost can add up if you decide to do the therapy. But the daily check ins are free!

This app broke after I got my subscription. It misses notifications for logging, closes at random, and I frequently get stuck in question loops when I track. Aside from that, the app is solely focused on depression and anxiety and doesn't look at other reasons why someone might have trouble getting things done, concentrating, or any number of things. If you're disabled or neurodivergent, the app is just going to continuously tell you that you're depressed. I regret my purchase very much.

Great concept, and very helpful! I had to uninstall the app for a brief period to free up space on my phone. I exported the data, as that feature was available. When I reinstalled the app and skimmed through the introduction/first assessment, I discovered that I could not important my exported profile data back to my account. This made me lose a LOT of progress. Personally, I believe you should not add the ability to export data if it cannot be loaded from the cloud, its a shame. Needs work.

Three months down! It's informative with explanations, suggestions, and resources. I recommend it as a great way to check in, learn/gauge your stressors, and see any patterns that might need adjusting. I'm going to try it for a while and see how it goes. I agree with the notifications not working properly. I get one I'd be lucky. It would be beneficial to add a "I don't know" or "sometimes" as an option or a few more prompts to help describe difficult situations. Thanks!

When it works as intended, very useful! However it often does not actually record entries, especially on stressful/bad days, and then gives you the message that you need more entries for a more accurate result... I've even uninstalled and redownload and the issue does not fix. Worse, it sometimes effects later entries and thus your day looks better/worse than it actually was. This issue has been off and on over the years of me having this app, but has gotten far worse recently..

I haven't answered enough to get a report yet, but the daily questions are helpful to get an idea of what your mindset is throughout the day. There are also some good little articles that go over different illness and thinking patterns that are pretty informative, and some have exercises that are intended to help you learn coping skills. I have high hopes for the app, but premium features are around $25 every three months. Seems a little steep.

They are adding features over time to make it easier to track why I am in a good or bad mood. Even though they haven't added those features yet, for now, just tracking my mood over time helps me spot likely depression. While you could keep a paper journal to do the same, this program prompts you for input, so I am more likely to remember to track my mood. While I already know the info in the little blurbs, they do also have short tutorials on the importance of exercise, etc.

It's good as a habit tracker and mood tracker. There is an option for online therapy, but it's a redirect to a website. I would not buy premium, one because if the trial exercise is anything to go by, the resources aren't that good quality, and there's really not much else that premium does but unlock the exercises, and two the amount of money is absurd. The assessment is okay I guess, but the amount of questions they ask doesn't get that much of a reliable result.

I've been using this app since mid December of 2019. It is the only self care app I have been able to be consistent with, including journals. Having mood tracking data is very helpful for ascertaining trends and sharing them with my psychiatrist. It would be even more helpful if I made notes of what I was experiencing during each check in, which there is an option for. I have not utilized the courses or paid for Plus to unlock more, but I imagine they are more potential help to be accessed.

Pretty good. At first couldn't figure out how to answer questions because you have to slide this little white (hard to see) tab upwards if you're in Calendar mode. Secondly, I just wish it had more stuff that was free to help. I don't mind paying but the prices are quite high too for 10 minute modules of basic techniques. I just wish there was more for if you answer questions and are in a crisis. Like a mode to help calm you in a panic attack or a chat for when you're really depressed.

There needs to be a way to adjust when you get reminders. I get my evening reminder at 6:30. I'm usually not even home by then, so getting the notification so early is pointless. I usually try and wait to fill it out right before I go to bed, so it would be great if I could get the reminder 5 hours later. It's a huge flaw amd it drives me crazy. It would also be nice if you could adjust the displayed experiences/emotions instead of having to type things in every time.

Honestly my favorite mood tracker app. I love the questions and how it reminds you 3 times a day, my favorite part is the pauses though. Now for criticisms- my biggest thing is not having a full list of all preset emotions and situations to view. The little sample size they give you is limited and then you have to try and search for others by just guessing and seeing if the creators thought to put it in there. I would much prefer the option to have a menu with all of them available somewhere.

Great app. It allows me to get a better handle on how to take action. The only downside from the most recent update are the notifications. The clock seems to be off by at least 5 hours. My 6am notification never alerted me, I just happened to notice at 7am. When I went to check the countdown clock, it had roughly 4 hours left before the first notification.

I dont know how I got to downloading this app or how I even got to using it 3 times a day. it really puts things in a simple perspective for one to be able to reflect on and maybe see where you go wrong or right in your day to try to learn and improve. its quick and simple, and you can be as involved or as uninvolved as you want with the apps other additives. just try it.

I like the app and use it every day. Overall it's great, only thing I wish is there was a way to see more emotions and situations instead of a handful fo defaults or having to search. I have no idea what other ones are offered and would rather try and fit it to what they have, then have to come up with one myself every other time. I find this inhibits my use of the situation section. for emotions it's not as big a deal but still would want to see the other options.

I've used the free parts of this app for a while, and it's really helpful for keeping track of how I'm doing. Even just reflecting on my feelings helps me deal with them better, I think. I recently paid for the courses since I liked a meditation on self-compassion a lot. I'm definitely glad I did -- there's some great reading and supplemental work to my therapy. Desired improvements: 1) reminders of practice assignments from courses I've read, and 2) meditation audio while phone is locked.

It's really helpful and I like tracking my day but the questions you get in the morning, day and night don't all give you reminders for when it's time to answer them. If you're not thinking about it or checking it you could miss your questions and you can't go back and answer them after the allotted time is up. You get notifications for the morning questions but not afternoon or night and there's no setting to receive them. To me it's a big issue because I end up with big gaps.

It's ok an app is not free, but I don't like an app that most of the content aren't free but listed it as a free app (they replied to one comment stated that most are free, out of 4 categories, Pause is completely paid feature; in Discovery out of 8 courses only 1 is free, all excercises are paid feature, that's 2 categories, their defenition of "most" is different from mine) It feels they think it's ok to waste people's time as long as having more chances to lure you in for subscription. Pass.

This app is excellent for its intended purpose. I was looking for an easy way to track my mood to have a written history so that I could better see problems and solutions and their results. It is sooo easy to use and well made. The only slight change preference would be to be able to login and have a corresponding website so that I could sync progress across devices. Right now you can download results from your device but not sync across devices. However, if that would mean ads don't do it lol.

Great for setting patterns and stressors. It's a simple interface that shows you when you're most affected by any lows in your week or day. There's a notes section that is helpful to document why you're feeling how you are. This includes good times and days (most of mine are weekends). At the end of the week you get a review. There's also helpful information and exercises for relaxation and mindfulness but I haven't used them. Update: the latest updates made this app great for tracking mood!

I coincidentally downloaded MindDoc right before beginning my therapy journey 4 years ago. It has been very cool to see it develop and grow over time. I've never used the "extras" much. I'm a data person, so I've always been very consistent with the check-ins. Every so often, I take the results to therapy to show off how things have changed and that has been SO rewarding! This app didn't make those changes happen, but it helped me notice trends and patterns to help myself make them happen. :)

So far, so good. I've only been using Moodpath for about a week, but it helps me to really see where my low lows are and just a "normal" low. I'd recommend it. I've read a couple of the extra things they provide and they were good, but I'm honestly just using it for the mood tracker. You can set the reminders to what time works for you which is great. I'd recommend it, especially if you're trying to keep track depression lows and how bad they get before you feel that you're out of them.

Only had it a few days, but so far I love it. I have a bullet journal and I try to track my moods by coloring the day to match the "mood" on my calendar, but when you're depressed, sometimes getting the supplies out and journaling/coloring is too much to bother with. This app is the same concept, but it seriously simplifies the process. It also reminds you to fill out your day (if you want it to) I also love the facts and tips about depression, not only to learn more about it myself, but to use their facts to explain my situation to loved ones, because I know they struggle with my depression, but I never have the right words to explain it all.

Even if you do not intend to share your results with a therapist, they help you identify emotions and feelings that you need to overcome to be able to pick yourself up and challenge. Journaling did not come easy at first but I find myself opening the app to use it more times a day to make an entry than what it reminds me to do. I am recommending this app to others and I work in mental healthcare.

This app is super helpful, professional, and super easy. I can't tell you how many apps I've tried over the years, to help you track your mood or keep a journal. I've always sucked at sticking with that kind of thing. After a few days I'm done. But this is simple & easy. I started using this app to help track my moods and symptoms for my therapists after severe trauma. It tracks everything and writes a summary of your mental health for you let doctors, as well as giving you insights to improve.

Its a pretty cool app. I do like being able to analyze the patterns in my mood and really reflect on how im feeling. The questions get a bit repetitive and sometimes seem irrelevent to me. And i dont know if 3 questions at a time is enough to really measure a persons mood. But i do like being able to pick the scale of how im feeling and write down notes. It gives me a chance/reminder to write out my feelings like a mini journal. Overall, i like it

I have tried several mood apps and low tech paper trackers... I like this one because it checks in throughout the day and my mood fluctuates throughout the day. It's also only 3 questions -- they're very direct yes/no and then rated in terms of severity. I also appreciate data tracking or recognizing trends and the app does so in a color coded way. Visually it appears clear and not overwhelming.

It's a helpful app. They explain the link between emotions, thoughts, and depression. I like the meditation guides. very helpful and they take it slow by teaching you one small bit at a time. I wish they would add the Journaling feature to the Insight section where they summarize your weekly mood entries. Sometimes, the Insight says 'think and write about something good that happened yesterday'. I wish I could just make my notes on that screen.

I would highly recomend, has many insights that were good to read/listen to. Only bad thing is somehow whether on my end or develpers' end? Had to start over which is maybe a good thing so can see if I get the same or similar results. More time in now and am very pleased with the app. I entered into a study of depression through the app. Wasn't really keen on the idea of my location, travel habits etc. being tracked but may help myself and others and is voluntary and can quit at any time.

Love this app except for one thing... Whenever I try to create an account, it doesn't let me create/type a password hence making me unable to make an account. I had to factory reset my tablet so I wanted to save my journal entries, alas I couldn't without an account. Pretty sad about that, but this app is really good for reminding yourself you have feelings. Sometimes life gets too busy that you forget about your emotions. Helped me cope while I found the right therapist for me.

Seems great but only people with expendable income could possibly use it... The kind of people that buy Starbucks every day. Far too expensive, and I'm very disappointed that all the apps I find are trying to make money off of sad and desperate people. It would be much cheaper to buy a freaking book, which I'll probably end up doing. This seems like it would be beneficial, but I can't get ONE course for free.. like nothing. No free content. Middle finger up with all the enthusiasm.

I am desperate to control my symptoms and thus far this is the BEST app that I've found that monitors your entire specteum of depression and anxiety. It also has a knowledge base that is easy for the layperson. You can follow your progress in real time. The ONLY problems that I could find are that you can't backtrack if you make a mistake and since most people are depressed who use it...injecting a bit of humor wouldn't hurt;-)

Best, most important app I've ever had! It never fails to help me through my daily struggles and there's always new things to learn. Highly recommended to anyone that needs help understanding emotions of themselves or others. There are tons of articles to read or listen to that give you insight and awareness about the positive and negitive things in your life and how to deal with it, along with music and activities designed to relieve stress. Love it!

It's really helpful to track your mood through the day and see an overview of how you've been feeling. The only thing I would perhaps change is having an expanded checklist for the emotions and situations instead of having to search for ones not presently listed. Or being able to choose which emotions and situations are constantly shown.

I kept forgetting to use this so my progress kept resetting. I'm back in the swing now and it feels kinda good to just sort of journal my thoughts in a way. Just wished when I said I woke up at 7, it didn't send me notifications at 7. It's like "come on guys, I'm still waking up". But I changed the recorded time so I can actually experience my day before I answer questions. It really did help me sort of tell when I had a depression coming on. I'm hoping it can help me keep track of coming growth

Exceeded my expectations with their results after I consistently answered questions up to three times a day. I definitely feel like the questions and results from which are relevant and versatile. I really like all of the helpful articles and it kind of feels like a mini course and they have it broken up into several articles and prompts to answer that really got you engaged and deeper in thought.

Wow. Cannot believe you've locked the basic bare bones feature of viewing mood history behind your $100/year paywall. I would happily pay a one time price for a premium app, but there's no way I can afford that absurdly expensive subscription model. What is the point of a mood journal app if you can't look back and see your old entries?? I was worried this app would go south when it got bought out. I guess I was right. New users beware, don't waste your time, it's all downhill from here.

Very impressed with the app interface and the way the AI learns about my specific needs.

I am not a person to usually write reviews at all but this app blew me away. You are getting 300 dollars worth of therapy and more for only 4 dollars... I was extremely against using AI as a therapist but its even better than a therapist it cares more and is more interested and gives you things to think about . This is a very helpful and useful app, especially for people who are budget conscious and do not want to spend hundreds of dollars on traditional therapy. The guided meditations are especially good in that they provide the right balance of structure and relaxation that allows the user a few minutes of tranquility in an increasingly hectic and (often) chaotic world. As someone who has been resistant to incorporating AI into my life, using this app felt natural and easy. I am newer to guided mediations and I was initially skeptical about the use of AI. Receive weekly reports analyzing your recordings over the past week. Recognize and reflect on your emotional fluctuations and trends to better understand yourself. Statistical data provides further objective self-analysis, aiding in self-discovery and long-term life planning.
